newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIAN POLICE CLAIM PROGRESS AGAINST CORRUPTION.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIAN POLICE CLAIM PROGRESS AGAINST CORRUPTION.

text.p: Romanian police said they were making progress fighting rampant corruption and economic crimes under a cleanup drive launched by the country's new centrist government.
Bucharest police chief Virgil Ardeleanu said on Thursday his force was dismantling gangs responsible for millions of dollars of lost state revenue through smuggling and tax evasion.

He made his comments amid a blaze of publicity given to investigations launched against high-profile post-Communist businessmen alleged to have cost state coffers huge sums by flouting banking, accounting and trade laws.
"We have been hitting criminal structures for a month. We see a real chance to restore order in the economic, financial and banking sectors," Ardeleanu told a news conference.
"This means returning to the state budget billions of lei (millions of dollars) siphoned into the pockets of various officials through evasion and smuggling."
Like most ex-communist countries, Romania has been beset by an explosion of crime, with corruption and white collar infractions a major political issue.

Reformist President Emil Constantinescu, who defeated an ex-communist in last November's election, has made the fight against corruption a priority in his bid to right the Balkan country's sagging economy and boost living standards.
In the past month, a string of prominent entrepreneurs have been put under investigation for corruption.

Razvan Temesan, head of the state-run bank Bancorex, was sacked and an enquiry launched into alleged irregularities under his stewardship. Another bank president was jailed and several executives arrested in the past two years for fraud.

The general prosecutor on Thursday launched procedures to lift the parliamentary immunity of a deputy from the former ruling Party of Social Democracy who is to be investigated for alleged frauds worth the equivalent of more than $11 million.

Earlier this week, police searched houses and offices belonging to George Constantin Paunescu, head of extensive local tourism and trade businesses, over allegations he illegally obtained a stake in a commercial bank.
Ardeleanu said there had been a 56 percent increase in economic crime in Bucharest alone in the first quarter of 1997.

Virgil Magureanu, head of the Romanian Intelligence Service, said last month that tax evasion had reached "frightening proportions" accounting for leakages of up to 38 percent of Romania's gross domestic product.
